title: Headron 3.62: chat evaluation and historical observations
scope: Historical local development observations and a controlled-prompt Codex proxy evaluation; not customer usage or proof of model improvement.

limitations: Scoring was unblinded and used a strict self-authored case key.
The baseline was likely contaminated by global agent instructions.
These sessions used a Codex proxy with tools disabled, not ordinary ChatGPT.
Differences do not establish causality or performance on unrelated tasks.
Deduplicated tool-use records; missing error flag does not prove success.
Verification classification is heuristic and does not establish passing tests.
Database item statuses are not independent verification or task-success measures.
The database is active; this is a historical sample.
Owner development events, not customer usage or independent task successes.
The recorded chain includes a historical break, and task attribution is incomplete.

interpretation: Do not sum these instruments: they overlap and measure different events. Preserve positive results and failure evidence, and verify actual task outcomes with clean baselines and independent blinded scoring.
